questions.question: What is net investment?

options.text: Sum of all the investments in a country

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gross investment - depreciation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A company's net investment is the sum of its expenditures on capital assets less the cost of depreciating those assets.
 
• This gives an idea of the actual spending on durable products utilized by the company in its operations, such as buildings, machinery, and software.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Depreciation: It means a fall in the value of an asset because of usage or with efflux of time or due to obsolescence or accident.
 
• Appreciation: It means an increase in the value of an asset over time. This the opposite of depreciation. It is an upward adjustment of the value of an asset held on a company's accounting book.
 
• Deceleration: It is the rate at which an asset's value in the market goes down.
 
• Gross investment: It is the total amount spent on goods in order to produce other goods and services. 
 
• Net investment: It is the amount of increase in productive stock.
 
• 
 
Capital investment is the money used by a business to purchase fixed assets, such as land, machinery, or buildings. The money may be in the form of cash, assets, or loans. Without capital investment, businesses may have a hard time getting off the ground.

• He was committed to fulfill the the dream of his father, Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata, an Indian Pioneer industrialist who founded the Tata Group.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The magnificent Kailasa temple at Ellora was built during the reign of which Rashtrakuta king?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kailasa temple:

 
 
• The Kailasha temple is also known as *Kailashanatha.*
 
• It is located at Ellora Caves in the Aurangabad District of Maharashtra.
 
• It was built by the 8th century Rashtrakuta King Krishna I.
 
• The time frame was nearly 756 to 773 AD.
 
• The temple is the largest of the rock-cut Hindu temples at the Ellora Caves.
 
• It is a megalith carved from a rock cliff face.
 
• It is considered one of the most remarkable cave temples in the world because of its size, architecture and sculptural treatment.
 
• The top of the superstructure over the sanctuary is 32.6 metres (107 ft) above the level of the court below. 
 
• Archaeologists believe it is made from a single rock.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Rashtrakuta Empire of Manyakheta was founded by Dantidurga (reigned 735-756 CE), also known as Dantivarman II.
 
• Gulbarga was the capital of his state.
 
• He was succeeded by his uncle Krishna I, who extended his kingdom throughout Karnataka.
 
• According to the Ellora record of Dantidurga, he conquered the Chalukyas in 753 and assumed the titles Rajadhiraja and Parameshvara.
 
• As per the Samangad inscription (modern Kolhapur district, Maharashtra), his mother was a Chalukyan princess from Gujarat named Bhavanaga.
 
• According to the same inscription, he defeated the invincible Karnata-Bala of the Badami Chalukyas.
 
• In addition, he defeated the kings of Lata (Gujarat), Malwa, Tanka, Kalinga and Sheshas (Nagas) in central India.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest artificial lake of Asia?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhopal Lake**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bhopal, known as the **"City of Lakes,**" boasts two prominent water bodies: the** Upper Lake (Bhojtal) and the Lower Lake (Chhota Talab).**
 
• **The Upper Lake**, built in the 11th century by King Bhoj, is a significant source of drinking water for the city. It's also a popular recreational spot, offering boating and scenic views.
 
• **The Lower Lake**, though smaller, contributes to the city's beauty. However, it faces pollution challenges due to urban and industrial activities.
 
• Together, these lakes form the Bhoj Wetland, a Ramsar site recognized for its ecological importance. Efforts are underway to preserve and restore the Lower Lake's ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Naini Lake**

 
 
• Uttarakhand CM Trivendra Singh Rawat__ has inaugurated the Naini lake water quality assessment system.
 
• It has been built at a cost of Rs 1 crore with UNDP assistance. 
 
• The water quality system will aid in water conservation and in keeping it clean.
 
• The State has successfully initiated a public movement to revive its rivers, lakes, ponds and water sources.
 
 
 
• Dal lake 
 
 
• It is an urban lake, which is the second largest in the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It is integral to tourism and recreation in Kashmir and is named the "Lake of Flowers", "Jewel in the crown of Kashmir" or "Srinagar's Jewel".
 
 
 
• **Chilika Lake **
 
 
• Chilika Lake is a brackish water lagoon located in the state of Odisha, India.
 
• It is the largest coastal lagoon in India and the second largest lagoon in the world.
 
• Chilika Lake is an important habitat for a variety of wildlife, including many species of birds, fish, and other aquatic animals.
 
• The lake is also a major tourist attraction and supports the livelihoods of local fishermen.

questions.question: Microbes like Rhizobium, Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter are used for:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**nitrogen cycling**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 Nitrogen Cycle-

 
 
• Nitrogen is an essential constituent of protein and is a basic building block of all living tissue. It constitutes nearly 16% by weight of all the proteins that is, converted to ammonia, nitrites or nitrates before it can be taken up by plants.
 
• Nitrogen fixation on earth is accomplished in three different ways:

 a) By microorganisms (bacteria and blue-green algae)

 b) By man using industrial processes (fertilizer factories) and

 c) To a limited extent by atmospheric phenomena such as thunder and lighting
 
• Certain microorganisms are capable of fixing atmospheric nitrogen into ammonium ions. These include free-living nitrifying bacteria (e.g. aerobic Azotobacter and anaerobic Clostridium) and symbiotic nitrifying bacteria living in association with leguminous plants and symbiotic bacteria living in non-leguminous root nodule plants (e.g. Rhizobium) as well as blue-green algae (e.g. Anabaena, Spirulina).
 
• Ammonium ions can be directly taken up as a source of nitrogen by some plants, or are oxidized to nitrites or nitrates by two groups of specialised bacteria: Nitrosomonas bacteria promote the transformation of ammonia into nitrite. Nitrite is then further transformed into nitrate by the bacteria Nitrobacter.
 
• The nitrates synthesised by bacteria in the soil are taken up by plants and converted into amino acids, which are the building blocks of proteins. These then go through higher trophic levels of the ecosystem. During excretion and upon the death of all organisms nitrogen is returned to the soil in the form of ammonia.
 
• Certain quantities of soil nitrates, being highly soluble in water, are lost to the system by being transported away by surface run-off or groundwater. In the soil as well as oceans there are special denitrifying bacteria (e.g. Pseudomonas), which convert the nitrates/nitrites to elemental nitrogen. This nitrogen escapes into the atmosphere, thus completing the cycle.
 
• The periodic thunderstorms convert the gaseous nitrogen in the atmosphere to ammonia and nitrates which eventually reach the earth’s surface through precipitation and then into the soil to be utilized by plants.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Carbon Cycle

 
 
• The carbon cycle involves several processes, including photosynthesis, respiration, decomposition, and combustion. Plants absorb carbon dioxide (CO₂) during photosynthesis, while animals release CO₂ through respiration.
 
• Carbon is stored in various reservoirs, including the atmosphere (as CO₂), oceans (as dissolved CO₂ and organic carbon), soil (as organic matter), and living organisms. These reservoirs play a crucial role in regulating global climate.
 
• Human activities, such as fossil fuel combustion and deforestation, significantly alter the carbon cycle by increasing atmospheric CO₂ levels, contributing to global warming and climate change.​
 
 
 
• Water Cycle-
 
 
• The hydrologic cycle is the continuous circulation of water in the Earth-atmosphere system which is driven by solar energy. Water on our planet is stored in major reservoirs like atmosphere, oceans, lakes, rivers, soils, glaciers, snowfields, and groundwater. Water moves from one reservoir to another by the processes of evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, deposition, runoff, infiltration, and groundwater flow.
 
• Water as an important ecological factor determines the structure and function of the ecosystem. Cycling of all other nutrients is also dependent upon water as it provides their transportation during the various steps. It acts as a solvent medium for their uptake of nutrients by organisms.
 
 
 
• Sulphur Cycle-
 
 
• The sulphur reservoir is in the soil and sediments where it is locked in organic (coal, oil and peat) and inorganic deposits (pyrite rock and sulphur rock) in the form of sulphates, sulphides and organic sulphur.
 
• It is released by weathering of rocks, erosional runoff and decomposition of organic matter and is carried to terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems in a salt solution.
 
• The sulphur cycle is mostly sedimentary except two of its compounds hydrogen sulphide (H2S) and sulphur dioxide (SO2) add a gaseous component to its normal sedimentary cycle.
 
• Sulphur enters the atmosphere from several sources like volcanic eruptions, combustion of fossil fuels, from the surface of the ocean and from gases released by decomposition. Atmospheric hydrogen sulphide also gets oxidised into sulphur dioxide.
 
• Atmospheric sulphur dioxide is carried back to the earth after being dissolved in rainwater as weak sulphuric acid.

questions.question: With reference to Sepoy Mutiny of 1857, on which of the following dates did the soldiers at Meerut start their journey to Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 May**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Sepoy Mutiny of the 1857 War of Independence started in Meerut city.
 
• Indian Mutiny, also called Sepoy Mutiny or First War of Independence, widespread but unsuccessful rebellion against British rule in India in 1857–59.
 
 
• Begun in Meerut by Indian troops (sepoys) in the service of the British East India Company, it spread to Delhi, Agra, Kanpur, and Lucknow.
 
• In India, it is often called the First War of Independence and other similar names.
 
• On 6th May 1857 A.D., 85 out of 90 Indian soldiers at Meerut refused to bite the greased cartridges with their teeth.
 
• These 85 soldiers were court-martialled and imprisoned for 10 years.
 
• They were stripped of their uniforms in the presence of the entire Indian crowd.
 
• The revolt spread over the entire area from the neighbourhood of Patna to the borders of Rajasthan.
 
• The Revolt of 1857 lasted for more than a year.
 
• It was suppressed by the middle of 1858.
 
• On July 8, 1858, fourteen months after the outbreak at Meerut, peace was finally proclaimed by Lord Canning.

questions.question: Purvanchal Himalayas does NOT comprise of:
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Pir Panjal range**

 
• The Pir Panjal Range is situated in the Kashmir region.
 
• It is named after the Pir Panjal Pass.
 
• Indrasan is the highest peak of Pir Panjal Range.
 
 
• Mount Indrasan is located at an altitude of 6221 meters above sea level.
 
• It is one of the most difficult mountains to climb.
 
 
 
• Deo Tibba and Indrasan are the major peaks of Pir Panjal range.
 
• The Kashmir valley lies between the Himadri and Pir Panchal range.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Purvanchal Range, or Eastern Mountains, is a sub-mountain range of the Himalayas in North-East India.
 
• The Purvanchal comprises :
 
 
• The Patkai Hills
 
• The Naga Hills
 
• Manipur Hills
 
• The Mizo Hills
 
 
 
• The Patkai Hills:
 
 
• The Patkai Hills are the hills on India's north-eastern border with Burma or Myanmar.
 
 
 
• The Naga Hills:
 
 
• The Naga Hills lie on the border of India and Burma.
 
 
 
• The Mizo Hills:
 
 
• Mizo Hills is a mountain range in southeastern Mizoram state.
 
• Mizo Hills form part of the north Arakan Yoma system.
 
 
 
• The range is an eastern extension of the Himalayan Range System, in northeastern India.
 
• It bends sharply to the south beyond the Dihang River gorge and spreads along the eastern boundary of India with Myanmar. 
 
• The Purvanchal includes the hill of the Patkai hills, Naga Hills, Mizo Hills, and Manipur hills.

• Helped promote the sport within the country and inspired future generations of players.

questions.question: In August 2022, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment launched the ________ scheme, with an aim to provide comprehensive rehabilitation services to people engaged in begging in 75 municipalities.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SMILE-75**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

SMILE-75 Initiative:

__
 
• Under the “SMILE-75” Initiative, 75 Municipal Corporations will undertake comprehensive rehabilitation of persons engaged in the act of begging in the spirit of Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav.
 
• Municipal Corporations, in collaboration with NGOs and other stakeholders, will cover several comprehensive welfare measures for persons who are engaged in the act of begging, with a focus extensively on rehabilitation, provision of medical facilities, counselling, awareness, education, skill development, economic linkages and convergence with other Government welfare programmes etc.
 
• The Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment has also allocated a total budget of Rs.100 crore for the SMILE project for the coming years till 2025-26.
 
• It seeks to develop a support mechanism for the holistic rehabilitation of those engaged in the act of begging.
 
• Implementing Ministry: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
 
• It includes the sub-scheme of Comprehensive Rehabilitation of persons engaged in the act of Begging.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• About Project "SMILE":

 
 
• SMILE: Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise.
 
• It is a new umbrella scheme that aims to provide welfare measures to the Transgender community and the people engaged in the act of begging.
 
• It was launched by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment on 12 August 2022.
 
• The Ministry has allocated Rs. 365 Crore for the scheme from 2021-22 to 2025-26.
 
• The Housing facility in the form of ‘Garima Greh’ ensures food, clothing, recreational facilities, skill development opportunities, recreational activities medical support, etc. to the Transgender community and the people engaged in the act of begging.
 
• The focus of the scheme is extensively on rehabilitation, provision of medical facilities, counseling, basic documentation, education, skill development, economic linkages, and so on.
 
• It is estimated that approximately 60,000 poorest persons would be benefited under this scheme for leading a life of dignity.

questions.question: Which is the National Mission for Financial Inclusion to ensure access to financial services, namely, a basic savings and deposits accounts, remittance, credit, insurance, pension in an affordable manner?

options.text: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana**

 
 
• Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) is a financial inclusion scheme launched by the Government of India.
 
• Its objective is to provide access to banking services to all households in the country.
 
• The scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on August 15, 2014.
 
• Under the scheme, any individual can open a savings or current account with zero balance.
 
• Account holders are also provided with a free debit card and an accident insurance cover of Rs 1 lakh.
 
• Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana has played an important role in promoting financial inclusion in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana

 
 
• It was launched by the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), Government of India in June 2011.
 
• It aims at creating efficient and effective institutional platforms of the rural poor, enabling them to increase household income through sustainable livelihood enhancements and improved access to financial services.
 
• It is aided in part through investment support from the World Bank. 
 
• In addition, the poor would be facilitated to achieve increased access to rights, entitlements, and public services, diversified risk, and better social indicators of empowerment.
 
• The blocks and districts in which all components of N.R.L.M are implemented are treated as ‘intensive’ blocks and districts, whereas the remaining as ‘non-intensive’ blocks and districts.
 
• In a typical intensive block, the first 3 years are spent building the organizations of the poor by mobilizing them into SHGs, Federations at Village, Cluster level, and Block levels.
 
 
 
• **Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana**

 
• Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana relates to the skill development of rural youth.

 
 
• Union government on 25 September 2014 launched Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana to train 1 million rural youths by 2017.
 
• It targets youth, in the age group of 15–35 years.
 
• It aims to provide them with jobs having regular monthly wages or above the minimum wages.
 
• It is a part of the National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM).
 
• National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM) is the Mission for poverty reduction called Aajeevika. 
 
• The Yojana was launched during the 98th birth anniversary of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay.
 
• Earlier the Yojana was known as Aajeevika Skills Development Programme (ASDP).
 
 
 
• **​Swaranjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana**
 
 
• The Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) was implemented at the beginning of the 1999–2000 fiscal year to replace six other related programmes.
 
• The initiative was created as a comprehensive plan to support rural impoverished people who work for themselves.
 
• It is funded by the Centre and the State in a 75:25 ratio and is implemented by commercial banks, regional banks and cooperative banks.

questions.question: Which of the following plays was NOT written by Harshavardhana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vikramorvasiyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Harshavardhana ruled from 606 - 647 AD.

 
 
• His earliest capital was Thaneswar.
 
• Harshavardhana (606-647 A.D.) ascended the throne of Thaneshwar and Kannauj on the death of his brother, Rajyavardhana.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Harshavardhana belonged to the Pushyabhuti dynasty.

 
 
• It was founded by Naravardhana close to the 5th or beginning of the 6th century A.D.
 
• The dynasty flourished under Prabhakarvardhana (father of Harshavardhana).
 
 
• He assumed the title of Maharajadhiraja.
 
 
 
• Harshavardhana succeeded the throne in 606 A.D.
 
• Harsha was also known as Sakalottarapathanatha.
 
• He conquered Magadha.
 
• He established his capital at Kannauj.
 
• His empire extended from Punjab to northern Orissa and from the Himalayas to the bank of Narmada.
 
• The period of Harsha is well documented in Harshacharitra written by Banabhatta.
 
• Chinese scholar Hiuen-Tsang visited Harsha's court in 631 A.D.
 
• The empire came to an end along with the death of Harshavardhana in 647 A.D.
 
• Harshavardhan wrote three Sanskrit plays viz. Nagananda, Ratnavali and Priyadarshika.
 
• Hiuen-Tsang mentioned the grand assembly held at Kannauj in 643 A.D. which was attended by twenty kings, four thousand Buddhist monks and about three thousand Jains and Brahmans.
 
• He also organised Mahamoksha Harishad, a religious festival, at Prayaga (Allahabad).

questions.question: The organisms that do not have a defined nucleus or organelles are classified in to ______ Kingdom.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Monera**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Monera kingdom:

 
 
• These organisms lack a defined nucleus or organelles and none of them has multicellular bodies.
 
• Some of them have cell walls while some do not.
 
• This group of species may either synthesize their own food (autotrophic) or obtain it from the environment (heterotrophic).
 
• Bacteria, blue-green algae (cyanobacteria), and mycoplasma are examples.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fungi kingdom:

 
 
• These are heterotrophic eukaryotic organisms. 
 
• Some of them are known as saprotrophs, which feed on decaying organic matter.
 
• Others feed on the living protoplasm of a host organism. They are called parasites.
 
• Many of them have the capacity to become multicellular organisms at certain stages in their lives.
 
• Their cell walls are made of chitin, a tough complex sugar.
 
• Examples are yeasts, moulds, and mushrooms.
 
 
 
• **Protista** kingdom
 
 
• Protista kingdom single-celled eukaryotes.
 
• Characteristics of Protista are given bellow:
 
 
• Unicellular organism.
 
• Normally aquatic.
 
• Reproduction: Asexual & sexual.
 
• Well defined nucleus & membrane-bounded organelles.
 
 
 
• Group of Protista are given bellow:
 
 
• Prokaryotic: Dinoflagellate, Diatoms, Euglenoids.
 
• Consumer: Slime moulds, Myxomycetes.
 
• Protozoans: Slime moulds, Myxomycetes.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Plantae**
 
 
• Kingdom plantae includes all eukaryotic, chlorophyll-containing organisms called plants.
 
• Some of these members are primarily heterotrophic, such as insectivorous plants or parasites.
 
• Kingdom plantae is divided into 5 major divisions:
 
 
• Algae (Thallophyta)
 
• Bryophytes
 
• Pteridophytes
 
• Gymnosperms and
 
• Angiosperms
 
 
 
• 
 
Algae (Thallophyta)

 
 
• Algae are chlorophyll-containing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and largely aquatic (both freshwater and marine) organisms.
 
• Algae are self-feeders.
 
• 
 
Bryophytes

 
 
• The bryophytes are generally classified into two main groups
 
• Liverworts
 
 
• Liverworts usually grow in moist, shady places such as banks of streams, marshy ground, damp soil, the bark of trees, and deep in the woods.
 
 
 
• Mosses
 
 
• Mosses grow in dense mats over moist shady places, especially during rainy seasons.
 
 
 
• 
 
Pteridophytes

 
 
• Pteridophytes are primitive seedless vascular plants also called cryptogams.
 
• The pteridophytes are found in cool, damp shady places though some may flourish well in sandy-soil conditions.
 
• 
 
Gymnosperms

 
 
• Gymnosperms are vascular plants having naked seeds.
 
• The gymnosperms are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilisation.
 
• 
 
Angiosperms

 
 
• Angiosperms are seed bearing plants or flowering plants.
 
• Unlike gymnosperms where the ovules are naked, in angiosperms the sporophylls are organized into flowers and seeds are produced inside fruits,

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides that 'there shall be a Vice President of India'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 63**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Article 63**

 
 
• Article 63 of the Indian Constitution states that "There shall be a vice president of India."
 
 
• The vice president acts as president in the absence of the president due to death, resignation, impeachment, or other situations.
 
 
 
• The vice president of India is also ex officio chairperson of the Rajya Sabha. When a bill is introduced in Rajya Sabha, the vice president decides whether it is a financial bill or not.
 
 
• If he is of the opinion, a bill introduced in the Rajya Sabha is a money bill, he would refer the case to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha for deciding it.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Article 61**
 
• The process for the impeachment of the President is outlined in Article 61 of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
• Either House of Parliament may file the impeachment accusations.
 
• The President must be notified 14 days in advance, and these allegations must be signed by one-fourth of the House members who framed them.
 
• The other House, which is tasked with conducting an investigation into the allegations, receives the impeachment resolution when it has been approved by a two-thirds majority of the entire membership of that House.
 
• The President has the right to show up and be represented during such an investigation.
 
• The President is removed from office as of the date the resolution is passed if the other House concurs with the accusations and approves the impeachment resolution with a two-thirds majority of its members.
 
• Impeachment is a quasi-judicial process in Parliament as a result.
 
 
 
• In this context, it is important to keep in mind two things:
 
 
• nominated members of either House of Parliament may take part in the impeachment of the President even though they did not cast a ballot in his election;
 
• and elected members of state legislative assemblies and the union territories of Delhi and Puducherry may not, even though they cast a ballot in the President's election.
 
 
 
• **Article 65**
 
 
• Article 65 deals with the Vice-President acting as President or discharging the functions of the President in the event of a vacancy.
 
 
 
• ​Article 62
 
 
• **Article 62 **of the Indian Constitution deals with the time frame for holding an election to fill a vacancy in the office of the **President.**

questions.question: The green revolution technology resulted in an increase in production of cereal production from 72.4 million tons in 1965-66 to _______ million tons in 1978-79.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**131.9**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The green revolution is the rise in agricultural productivity, particularly in developing nations, made possible by the use of novel crops and farming techniques.
 
• Given that he started the Green Revolution in India, M. S. Swaminathan is regarded as its father. He was motivated by Norman Borlaug's effort.
 
• Norman Borlaug started the Green Revolution movement in the 1960s. He is referred to as the "Father of the Green Revolution" globally. For his efforts in creating High Yielding Varieties (HYVs) of wheat, it resulted in him being awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.
 
• In order to enhance food production and reduce hunger and poverty, high-yielding cultivars of rice and wheat were first introduced in India in the 1960s.
 
• In Punjab, the Green Revolution in India was first implemented in late 1966 or early 1967 as a part of a development initiative launched by international donor organisations and the Indian government.
 
• One of the innovative techniques created during the Green Revolution was drip irrigation. This technology allowed water to drop slowly and steadily to the roots of plants, saving water and promoting more sustainable agriculture.
 
• India has achieved significant progress thanks to the Green Revolution, which has brought about a previously unheard-of level of food security. It has helped many non-poor people avoid the poverty and hunger they would have otherwise faced while lifting a significant number of poor people out of poverty

questions.question: Calculate the oxidation number of 'S' in H₂S₂O₇.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's denote the oxidation number of sulfur as 'x'.
 
• In H₂S₂O₇:
 
• Hydrogen (H) has an oxidation number of +1.
 
• Oxygen (O) has an oxidation number of -2.
 
• The overall charge of the molecule is 0.
 
• So, we can set up the equation: 
 
• 2(+1) + 2(x) + 7(-2) = 0
 
• Simplifying:
 
• 2 + 2x - 14 = 0
 
• 2x = 12
 
• x = +6 
 
• Therefore, the oxidation number of sulfur (S) in H₂S₂O₇ is **+6.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an amendment made to the Airport Economic Regulatory Authority (AERA) Amendment Act, 2021?

options.text: The government can call any airport a major airport just by notification.
The government will club together profit-making and loss-making airports.
The government can offer airports as a package in PPP mode to the prospective bidders.
A major airport is one which has an annual traffic of minimum 35 lakh passengers.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A major airport is one which has an annual traffic of minimum 35 lakh passengers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On March 24, 2021, the Lok Sabha received the Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India (Amendment) Bill, 2021.
 
• The 2008 Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India Act is being modified.
 
• The Airport Economic Regulatory Authority was founded under the 2008 Act.
 
• AERA regulates tariffs and other charges (such as airport development fees) for aeronautical services rendered at major airports in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A major airport is one that receives at least 35 lakh passengers annually, according to the 2008 Act.
 
• Any airport may be designated as a major airport by notification from the federal government.
 
• According to the Bill, the federal government may group airports and declare the group to be a major airport.
